page.layout: One page of running text in one column; marginal notes in the left margin.

main_text.p: hortatur[?] Apostolus. Nox praecessit, dies autem appropinquavit; Abiiciamus igitur opera tenebrarum, & induamur habitu, qui luci convenit, & Rom.13. [illegible, ~20 letters] Christiani simus Peripatetici, & sicut in die decenter ambulemus, non in comessationibus & ebrietatibus, non in cubilibus & lasciviis, non in lite & invidia, sed induamini Domino Iesu Christo, & carnis curam ne habeatis ad explendas cupiditates. Vltima autem ista verba cum sustulisset librum, & legisset Augustinus, pconfess.l.8 c.12 coelesti quadam metamorphosi, e fluctuante Rhetore & distractio Philosopho, constantissimus evasit Sanctus. Unde constat, quod abstinere corpus a superfluo huiusmodi malle, est reficere, & quasi animare animam.[illegible, ~7 letters] Iejunus Seruator aggreditur & fugat Satanam: Iejunans & orāti Cornelio, apparuit ubipelus[?] Evangelicus: valde esuriens Petrus, cum coelum ipsi aperiebatur, & in demisso linteo, & missis animalibus, revelatum erat illi de vocatione Gentium Mysterium. Exemplar demum se praebet proprij praecepti Doctor Gentium ὑπωπιάζω μου τὸ σῶμα καὶ[?] δουλαγωγῶ, continuando corpus meum & in Servitutem redigo, ne forte cum aliis praedicaverim, ipse Re-probus.I.Cor. 9.

page.notes: Printed text: the running head reads "Contio habita". The margin notes "Matth. 4." and "Act. 10. / Ibid." are printed beside the fasting and Cornelius lines, and the note beside "huiusmodi" is not legible enough to read. The Greek in the last column is near the limit of legibility: the middle word is uncertain, and the closing accent marks are uncertain. Line 1 and the start of line 4 are damaged and overprinted where the text was hard to read.
